title: Pick the next strategy to test
why: Research ranked late-day momentum (last 30 minutes follow the day's direction, driven by forced hedging) first, gap fade second, jump reversal third.
recommendation: Test late-day momentum on MES first with bare rules, plus a matched random-direction benchmark. Decide its $/day goal before seeing results.

title: Close SC-FUT-0002 (late-day momentum) as not demonstrated?
why: On 2019-2024 practice data it lost money after costs on MES (-$3.93/day) and roughly broke even on MNQ (-$0.45/day). The direction signal was only slightly better than random (+$2-3/day, not significant).
recommendation: Close it. Don't chase the volatile-days slice that looked better: that would be picking a winner after the fact.

title: Pre-register the prop size for SC-FUT-0005 (before the exam)
why: SC-FUT-0006 (high-volatility days only, 3 MNQ) failed: the calm days were the better half. Trading SC-FUT-0005 every day looked better in the simulator at 2-3 MNQ (no-lock rules: 48% / 43% first-account pass vs 17% luck; median 72 / 55 trading days), but those sizes were seen after results, so only the locked 2025-26 exam can judge one.
recommendation: Pre-register ONE every-day size (2 or 3 MNQ) and orders within 5 s of each check, then spend one exam check on it. Or add markets first.

title: SC-FUT-0005 can't pay out within 2 months: choose the next direction
why: Under every frozen sizing rule it loses $105-212 over 42 days (mostly fees). Only 1.5-5% of runs reach a payout. It beats luck, but its ~$11 per contract per day is too slow to pass the $3,000 Combine and earn payout days in 2 months, and bigger sizes break the risk limit.
recommendation: Don't spend the exam check. Either accept a longer window (about 3-4 months) for this strategy, or look for a faster/bigger edge (more markets, or several same-day rules on the data we own).
